title: OAGRC solicitation spec — the OUTBOUND artifact, validated before anything is sent
description: What a party will be asked, frozen and hashed before a single token is spent. This is NOT solicitation.schema.json, which describes the summary written AFTER a run and requires k_collected, raw_samples and variance — fields that cannot exist yet. Validating an outbound spec against the inbound schema was proposed and rejected in review: it would have failed every spec for lacking fields it is not the spec's job to have, and the natural repair is to weaken the check.

party_key.description: The short handle used in filenames only. NOT the party's identity. Hyphens are permitted so a capability-bearing party can be named for its capability (`gemini-fetch-v1`), which D-09 requires: the same weights with a different capability is a different party.

identity.description: The canonical identity published in the record. D-09's never-merge rule: a routed API identity is not the chat-surface identity of a similarly named system, and an abbreviation like 'gpt' invites exactly that merge.

question_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the EXACT UTF-8 bytes of the proposing party's question, before any normalisation. Whitespace-collapsed lowercased keys were used first; case and spacing can be substantive, so the identity of a question is its bytes.

temperature.description: Must exceed zero. At temperature 0 the k samples are one sample repeated, and a distribution computed over them is a number that looks like variance and is not.

context_pack.description: What the party was shown besides the question, and the hash that makes two rounds' packs comparable after the fact.

resolution.description: Rule-resolved, not fixed. The RULE is constant; the bytes it resolves to change as the repository changes, which is why the hash is pinned and checked rather than assumed.

web_search.description: The search capability frozen for this party in this round. A prompt that gives a party an address must also record whether that party could follow it — a citation you cannot resolve is not disclosure, and the record has to say which it was.

engine.description: Pinned to ONE engine across the panel. 'native' would route each provider to its own search backend, putting four different search engines inside one condition.

base_party_key.description: The tool-less party this one derives from. Recorded so a reader can SEE the relationship and so analysis cannot silently pool them: D-09 forbids merging a capability change onto the same identity, and this field makes the merge visible rather than preventing it.

capability.description: What this party could DO beyond emitting text. Frozen in the plan, never set by a flag: a CLI argument could diverge from the plan and the record would then describe a capability the party did not have.

entry_points.description: URLs named in the prompt. Anything else the party reached, it found.

search_web.description: Whether this party is given the search_web tool. SEPARATE from fetch_url: search discovers, fetch resolves, and a party holding one is not the party holding both under D-09.

k_solicited.description: Attempts SCHEDULED for this arm. Distinct from k_min_usable: the local arm schedules 6 for a floor of 5 because it loses ~1 sample in 120 (D-56). Overloading one number is what made the spare attempt buy nothing.

k_min_usable.description: Usable samples required. The citability floor, 5 for every party. The undersample gate and the published round page both test THIS, not k_solicited.

arm_id.description: An experimental condition, ORTHOGONAL to capability and party key. Two rounds can share a capability and differ in what the party was told to do with it; recording that on the capability suffix would conflate the two, which is what D-09 keeps apart.

arm_note.description: What the arm means for reading its statistics. For an instructed arm: tool-use incidence is intervention compliance, not exploration propensity, and is not comparable with a round that merely offered the tools.
